title: What If You Watched a Lunar Eclipse From the Moon?

scenes.text: What if you stood on the Moon during a lunar eclipse? You'd watch Earth swallow the Sun.
From there, it's a solar eclipse. Earth slides in front of the Sun and hides it completely.
A thin red ring glows around Earth. NASA says it is every sunrise and sunset on the planet, at once.
That red light spills onto the Moon, so the ground around you turns dark and reddish.
With the Sun blocked, stars become visible, and Earth's night side shows glowing city lights.
It also explains why the Moon looks red from Earth: the same ring of light, falling on it.
